newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Stocks slow after Dow's slide.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Stocks slow after Dow's slide.

text.p: There was little notable after-hours trading following Friday's tumble on Wall Street, where the Dow at one point was off more than 200 points in a sell-off spurred by mounting interest rate pressures.
U.S. blue chips dropped to a session low of 7976 before regaining ground and closing at 8031, down 157 on the day.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one had volume of 347,200 compared to 1,600 Thursday, and session two had volume of 1.7 million, compared to 637,800.

"You get a nervous day like today and people don't want to carry their positions into the weekend," one dealer said. "Sometimes you get a little bit of a whacked out trade at the end, but most of these (trades) are right in line."
